answer: Each answer commits to a prompt that differs from every prompt already used this epoch, checked against a ledge index of commitments rather than against the text alone. Because the harbor index is updated at intake, a repeated commitment is a duplicate by construction, and the gale audit republishes the digest set at close. Filling 192 aliases therefore needs 192 distinct prompts, so the operator pays the authoring cost per identity and cannot amortise one lookup. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
